Question Paper  
Exam Date & Time: 22-Dec-2025 (09:30 AM - 12:30 PM)  
  
  
  MANIPAL ACADEMY OF HIGHER EDUCATION  
  THIRD SEMESTER B.TECH. DEGREE EXAMINATIONS - DEC 25/JAN 26  
  SUBJECT: ECE 2124/ECE_2124 DIGITAL SYSTEM DESIGN  
  (SPL: ELECTRONICS AND COMMUNICATION ENGINEERING)  
  DIGITAL SYSTEM DESIGN [ECE 2124]  
Marks: 50                                                                                                       Duration: 180 mins.  
  
  A  
Answer all the questions.  
  
1A)               Design a combinational logic circuit with 4 inputs(A,B,C,D) and one output(Y), that will produce        (4)  
  output high if any three inputs are high. Implement the circuit using minimum number of NAND  
  gates.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1B)               Design a full adder circuit using two 2:1 multiplexers and additional gates by considering MSB of       (3)  
  inputs as selection line.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
1C)               Design a 4:16 decoder using 3:8 decoders with active low enable input.                                  (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2A)               Design a 3 bit synchronous Mod 5 counter using T flipflops.                                             (4)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2B)               Design a 4 bit asynchronous updown counter using positive edge triggered T Flipflops.                   (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
2C)               Design a BCD adder using two 4-bit adders and correction detector circuit. Illustrate with suitable     (3)  
  examples.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3A)               Design a sequential circuit using Mealy machine that can detect the overlapping sequence 1010.          (4)  
  Use positive edge triggered D flipflops.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO2" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
3B)               What is race-around condition in JK flipflops? Explain how Master Slave flipflop can solve race-        (3)  
  around condition with suitable logic diagram.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO1" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
3C)               Write a structural Verilog model for a 4-to-1 multiplexer using 2-to-1 multiplexer modules.             (3)  
  
  Page #1

Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4A)                   Write a behavioral Verilog code for a 4-bit Serial-In Serial-Out (SISO) shift register using positive    (4)  
  edge-triggered D flip-flops.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4B)                   Write dataflow modeling in Verilog to implement full subtractor.                                         (3)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
4C)                   Write a Verilog code to implement a 3-bit even parity generator using a user-defined primitive           (3)  
  (UDP).  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO3" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5A)                   Design and implement a 3-bit Johnson counter using the ACT-2 logic module.                               (4)  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5B)                   Realize the logic function                                                                               (3)  
  $$f(a,b,c,d)=Σm(0,2,6,7,10,14)$$  
  using a LUT-based FPGA where each LUT has 8-bit RAM.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Application"  
  
5C)                   Explain the Y-chart representation with respect to FPGA design. Discuss its three domains with           (3)  
  neat diagrams.  
  
  Course Outcome: "CO4" / Cognitive Level: "Understand"  
  
  
  -----End-----
